task_5.title: Guard shutdown after connection release
task_5.description: HTTPResponse.shutdown now fails explicitly when called after the response's connection has already been released back to the pool, preventing the released response from shutting down a connection that may have been reused by another response.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling HTTPResponse.shutdown on a response whose connection has already been released to the connection pool cannot silently close or corrupt a pooled connection that may be in use by another response.

expectation.grounded: HTTPResponse.shutdown must raise RuntimeError when the response no longer owns an active connection because it has been released to the pool. Existing ValueError behavior for responses without a socket shutdown handler must remain unchanged, and shutdown should continue to operate normally for responses that still own their connection.
expectation.conceptual: A response may only shut down the connection it still owns. Once that connection has been returned to the pool, shutdown must fail clearly instead of affecting pooled connection state or another active response.

constraints.grounded: The change must not alter normal HTTPResponse.shutdown behavior for attached, unreleased connections, must not change HTTPResponse.release_conn or drain behavior except for the subsequent shutdown outcome, and must preserve the existing error category for cases where socket shutdown support is unavailable.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be limited to preventing stale responses from interfering with pooled connections while preserving existing response lifecycle behavior for valid shutdown and release flows.

behavior: Calling HTTPResponse.shutdown after the response connection has been released to the pool raises RuntimeError.
A released response can no longer shut down the underlying socket for a connection that may have been reused by the pool.
Calling HTTPResponse.shutdown without an available socket shutdown handler continues to raise ValueError.
Calling HTTPResponse.shutdown while the response still owns its connection continues to shut down the read side of that connection.
acceptance_criteria: Given a response whose body has been drained and whose connection has been released to the pool, when HTTPResponse.shutdown is called on that response, it should raise RuntimeError.

Given a connection pool that reuses a released connection for a later response, when shutdown is called on the earlier released response, it should not terminate or corrupt the later response's connection.
Given a response that still owns its active connection and supports socket shutdown, when HTTPResponse.shutdown is called, it should perform the existing shutdown behavior.
Given a response that cannot perform socket shutdown because no shutdown handler is available, when HTTPResponse.shutdown is called, it should continue to raise ValueError.

task_6.title: Correct IPv6 CONNECT targets for proxy tunnels
task_6.description: urllib3 2.5.0 fixes proxy tunneling for HTTPS requests whose tunnel destination is an IPv6 literal, especially when the pool is created with connection_from_host. The CONNECT authority must preserve IPv6 bracket notation so proxies can parse the host and port correctly instead of rejecting the tunnel as malformed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that HTTPS proxy tunnels to IPv6 literal destinations created through urllib3 proxy connection APIs send a valid CONNECT authority with the IPv6 host enclosed in brackets, avoiding proxy connection failures caused by ambiguous host and port formatting.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3.connection.HTTPConnection performs a proxy tunnel for an IPv6 literal tunnel host on Python versions whose http.client does not already wrap IPv6 literals correctly, the CONNECT request target must bracket the IPv6 host before appending the port. This applies to proxy pools produced through ProxyManager.connection_from_host and must preserve existing behavior for already-bracketed IPv6 hosts, non-IPv6 hostnames, tunnel headers, response status handling, debug header output, and OSError behavior on non-OK tunnel responses.
expectation.conceptual: Applications using urllib3 or downstream clients should be able to open HTTPS connections through an HTTP proxy to IPv6 literal addresses without the proxy rejecting the tunnel because the destination address is malformed. Existing proxy behavior for IPv4 addresses and DNS names should remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: Do not double-wrap IPv6 hosts that already include brackets. Do not alter the proxy CONNECT authority for DNS names or IPv4 addresses. Do not change successful tunnel response handling, failure signaling for non-OK proxy responses, configured tunnel headers, or the Python versions whose standard library already provides correct IPv6 CONNECT formatting.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should be narrowly scoped to malformed IPv6 tunnel destinations and should not change how ordinary proxy connections, header forwarding, or error reporting work.

behavior: Proxy tunnel targets containing an IPv6 literal without surrounding brackets are normalized to use bracketed IPv6 authority syntax before the port is added.
Already bracketed IPv6 tunnel targets are left unchanged rather than being bracketed again.
Non-IPv6 tunnel targets, including hostnames and IPv4 addresses, continue to use their existing CONNECT target format.

On affected Python runtimes before the standard library fix, urllib3 supplies corrected tunnel formatting so ProxyManager.connection_from_host can establish HTTPS tunnels to IPv6 literal destinations.
For affected Python 3.12 runtimes, raw proxy response headers continue to be captured during CONNECT handling while using the corrected IPv6 authority formatting.
A proxy response other than successful tunnel establishment still closes the connection and raises the same tunnel failure signal as before.
acceptance_criteria: Given a proxy connection pool created with connection_from_host for an HTTPS IPv6 literal destination, when the tunnel is opened through an HTTP proxy, it should send a CONNECT authority where the IPv6 destination is bracketed and the port is outside the brackets.
When the IPv6 destination is already represented with brackets, opening the tunnel should not add another pair of brackets.
When the destination is a DNS name or IPv4 address, opening the tunnel should keep the existing host and port formatting.
When the proxy accepts the CONNECT request for an IPv6 literal destination, the HTTPS request should proceed instead of failing because the proxy could not parse the tunnel target.
When the proxy rejects the CONNECT request, urllib3 should continue to close the connection and surface the tunnel failure through the existing proxy error path.

task_3.title: Honor PoolManager redirect retry limits
task_3.description: urllib3 2.5.0 fixes a security-relevant redirect handling issue where a retry limit configured on PoolManager was not reliably applied while following redirects. Pool-level retry settings now participate in redirect exhaustion behavior, while per-request retry settings can still override the pool default.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that redirect limits configured through PoolManager retries are enforced when automatic redirects are followed, so callers can rely on pool-wide retry settings to cap redirect chains.

expectation.grounded: PoolManager must honor the retries parameter supplied at construction for redirect handling. Values accepted by Retry.from_int, including integer limits and False, and Retry instances should produce the corresponding observable redirect behavior. When a configured retry budget is exhausted while following redirects, PoolManager.request should raise MaxRetryError when redirect exhaustion is configured to raise; retries=False should continue to avoid raising a redirect exhaustion error. A retries value supplied directly to an individual PoolManager.request call remains the effective retry policy for that request.
expectation.conceptual: A client configured with a pool-wide redirect retry limit must consistently stop redirect chains at that limit. Disabling retries should remain a non-raising opt-out, and request-specific retry choices should still take precedence over the client default.

constraints.grounded: Do not regress existing PoolManager redirect behavior for callers without a pool-level retries configuration. Do not make retries=False behave like retries=0. Do not remove the ability for PoolManager.request retries to override the PoolManager default on a single request. Preserve MaxRetryError as the observable failure signal for redirect retry exhaustion.
constraints.conceptual: The fix should enforce configured safety limits without changing unrelated redirect behavior, without conflating disabled retries with zero allowed retries, and without removing per-request control.

behavior: A finite retries value configured on PoolManager now limits automatic redirect following instead of being bypassed by the redirect handling path.
Retry state is carried across redirect hops when no per-request retry policy is provided, so redirect counters and exhaustion behavior reflect the pool-level configuration.
Non-Retry pool-level retries values are interpreted as an effective Retry policy for redirects, with redirect exhaustion raising enabled unless retries is explicitly False.
retries=False at the PoolManager level remains a distinct opt-out that avoids raising MaxRetryError solely because a redirect would exceed a retry budget.
A retries value passed to an individual PoolManager.request call remains authoritative for that request and can be stricter or more permissive than the PoolManager default.
acceptance_criteria: Given a PoolManager configured with a finite retry budget and no per-request retry override, when a redirect chain exceeds that budget, it should stop by raising MaxRetryError instead of continuing under a default redirect policy.

Given a PoolManager configured with retries=0, when automatic redirect following would be required, it should treat the redirect budget as exhausted and raise MaxRetryError when redirects are enabled.
Given a PoolManager configured with retries=False, when a redirect response is encountered, it should not raise MaxRetryError solely due to redirect retry exhaustion.

Given a PoolManager configured with a restrictive pool-level retry limit, when a request supplies a more permissive retries value directly, that request should use the supplied retry policy for redirect handling.
Given no pool-level retries configuration and no per-request retries override, ordinary redirect handling should continue to behave as before.

task_2.title: Support hatch-vcs 0.5.0 for builds
task_2.description: The build configuration should accept hatch-vcs 0.5.0 so downstream builders and packagers can build the project in environments that provide the newer hatch-vcs release, instead of failing because only hatch-vcs 0.4.0 is accepted.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that source and wheel builds succeed when the build environment provides hatch-vcs 0.5.0, rather than requiring exactly hatch-vcs 0.4.0.

expectation.grounded: Project build metadata must allow hatch-vcs 0.5.0 as a valid build dependency for standard Python build workflows such as building a wheel without build isolation. A build environment with hatch-vcs 0.5.0 available should not report a missing dependency solely because hatch-vcs 0.4.0 is not installed.
expectation.conceptual: Users and downstream packagers should be able to build the project with the current hatch-vcs 0.5.x line without being blocked by an overly strict build dependency pin.

constraints.grounded: This change must remain limited to build-time dependency compatibility. It must not introduce any runtime dependency on hatch-vcs, change the package's public HTTP APIs, or alter installed runtime behavior.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should broaden build compatibility while preserving existing library behavior for users after installation.

behavior: Build dependency resolution accepts hatch-vcs 0.5.0 as satisfying the project's build requirements.
A no-isolation wheel build in an environment that has hatch-vcs 0.5.0 available no longer fails merely because hatch-vcs 0.4.0 is absent.
The change affects packaging and build-time behavior only; runtime library semantics remain unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Given a build environment with hatch-vcs 0.5.0 available, when a wheel build is started, then dependency resolution should accept that version and allow the build to proceed.
Given a build environment without hatch-vcs 0.4.0 but with hatch-vcs 0.5.0, when building without isolation, then the build should not fail due to a requirement for exactly hatch-vcs 0.4.0.
When the package is installed or imported after the build, it should expose the same runtime behavior and public APIs as before this build dependency compatibility change.

task_1.title: Support standard-library zstd on Python 3.14
task_1.description: urllib3 2.5.0 adds support for Python 3.14's standard-library zstandard module. zstd response decoding and zstd request advertising should work when compression.zstd is available, with the existing third-party zstandard package remaining as the fallback for older Python versions.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 can advertise and decode zstd-compressed HTTP responses on Python 3.14 using the standard-library zstandard support, without requiring the optional third-party zstandard package.

expectation.grounded: When Python's compression.zstd module is importable, urllib3 should enable zstd support, include zstd in urllib3.util.request.ACCEPT_ENCODING, and allow urllib3.response.ZstdDecoder and HTTPResponse decoding paths to process content-encoding: zstd bodies. If compression.zstd is not available, urllib3 should continue to use the PyPI zstandard package when it is present and new enough to expose the EOF state required for complete stream validation. Incomplete zstd payloads should continue to surface as urllib3.exceptions.DecodeError.
expectation.conceptual: Users on Python versions with built-in zstd support should get zstd HTTP compression support automatically. Users on older Python versions should keep the existing optional dependency behavior, and urllib3 should only advertise zstd when it can actually decode it.

constraints.grounded: Do not require the PyPI zstandard package when compression.zstd is available. Do not enable or advertise zstd when neither compression.zstd nor a compatible zstandard package is available. Preserve the existing requirement that third-party zstandard support must provide reliable EOF detection. Preserve DecodeError behavior for incomplete zstd streams and avoid changing unrelated content decoders such as gzip, deflate, or brotli.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add built-in Python zstd support without regressing existing compression behavior, without over-advertising unsupported encodings, and without weakening truncated-stream validation.

behavior: On runtimes where compression.zstd is available, zstd support is considered present even if the third-party zstandard package is absent.
compression.zstd is preferred over the PyPI zstandard package when both providers are available.
urllib3's advertised Accept-Encoding value includes zstd whenever either compression.zstd or a compatible zstandard package is available.
urllib3 can decode zstd-encoded HTTP response bodies through the standard response decoding path when compression.zstd is the active provider.
Zstd decoding continues to support multiple zstd frames in a single encoded payload by continuing through unused data after a completed frame.
Completing a zstd decode validates that the stream reached EOF and raises DecodeError for incomplete data.
On runtimes without compression.zstd, urllib3 falls back to the PyPI zstandard package only when its version supports the EOF state needed for validation.
acceptance_criteria: Given Python 3.14 or another runtime with compression.zstd available and no PyPI zstandard package installed, when urllib3 prepares its default accepted encodings, then zstd should be advertised.

Given Python 3.14 or another runtime with compression.zstd available, when an HTTPResponse is read with content-encoding set to zstd and a complete zstd body, then the response body should be transparently decompressed.

Given both compression.zstd and the PyPI zstandard package are available, when urllib3 determines zstd support, then the standard-library provider should take precedence while preserving the same user-visible decoding behavior.

Given compression.zstd is unavailable but a compatible PyPI zstandard package is installed, when urllib3 determines supported encodings, then zstd should still be advertised and zstd response decoding should continue to work.
Given neither compression.zstd nor a compatible PyPI zstandard package is available, when urllib3 determines supported encodings, then zstd should not be advertised as supported.
Given a truncated zstd-encoded response body, when urllib3 finishes decoding the response, then it should raise DecodeError rather than returning partial data as if the stream were complete.
Given a zstd-encoded response body containing multiple complete frames, when urllib3 decodes the response, then the decoded output should include the data from all frames in order.

task_4.title: Honor redirect controls in Node.js Emscripten runtime
task_4.description: The Node.js Emscripten fetch runtime should allow urllib3 to control redirect handling so request options such as retries and redirect are respected instead of being bypassed by the JavaScript fetch layer.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that urllib3 requests made from the Node.js Emscripten runtime respect user-supplied redirect and retry settings when a response redirects.

expectation.grounded: When urllib3 runs through its Emscripten fetch transport under Node.js, redirect responses must be exposed to urllib3's own redirect handling so public APIs such as urllib3.request and PoolManager.request honor the retries and redirect parameters. Redirect-enabled requests should continue to follow redirects according to urllib3 semantics, redirect-disabled requests should return the original redirect response, and exhausted redirect retry budgets should surface urllib3's standard redirect exhaustion behavior.
expectation.conceptual: Users running urllib3 in Node.js-backed WebAssembly environments should get the same observable redirect behavior they requested through urllib3 options, rather than having redirects handled automatically by the underlying runtime.

constraints.grounded: The change must be scoped to Node.js detection within the Emscripten fetch runtime and must not alter browser behavior where urllib3 cannot control redirects in the same way. Existing non-redirect request behavior and normal successful redirect following must remain compatible with urllib3's established APIs.
constraints.conceptual: Do not regress redirect behavior in browsers or for ordinary requests; only make Node.js honor the caller's redirect-related configuration.

behavior: In the Node.js Emscripten runtime, 3xx redirect responses are made available to urllib3 instead of being automatically followed before urllib3 can apply its options.
The redirect parameter on urllib3 request APIs controls whether a redirect response is followed or returned to the caller in Node.js.
The retries parameter on urllib3 request APIs applies to redirect handling in Node.js, including the behavior when no redirect retries remain.
Default redirect behavior continues to follow redirects according to urllib3 semantics when redirects are enabled.
Browser Emscripten behavior remains unchanged because the redirect-control adjustment is specific to Node.js.
acceptance_criteria: Given a urllib3 request running in the Node.js Emscripten runtime and receiving a redirect response, when redirects are enabled, it should follow the redirect using urllib3's redirect handling.

Given a urllib3 request running in the Node.js Emscripten runtime and receiving a redirect response, when redirect is disabled, it should return the redirect response to the caller instead of following it.

Given a urllib3 request running in the Node.js Emscripten runtime and receiving a redirect response, when the redirect retry budget is exhausted, it should report redirect exhaustion consistently with urllib3's normal retry behavior.
Given urllib3 is running in a browser Emscripten runtime, redirect behavior should remain consistent with the pre-existing browser limitations.
Given a non-redirecting request in the Emscripten fetch runtime, behavior should remain unchanged.
